text: {"reconstruction":4,"feasibility":3,"rationale":"The proposal gets the core procedure right (caniuse lookup, MDN search and URL, then To, Subject and Body in the mail draft), but it ends with \"Send\" when the true workflow says never to send and to discard the draft and close the MDN tab. It also has a redundant recipient_name parameter (the true workflow derives the email as {customer}@example.com), omits the new-tab and tab-switching steps, and leaves the \"not supported\" case and the {version} extraction vague, so an automation built from it could mistakenly send the email."}

data.rationale: The proposal gets the core procedure right (caniuse lookup, MDN search and URL, then To, Subject and Body in the mail draft), but it ends with "Send" when the true workflow says never to send and to discard the draft and close the MDN tab. It also has a redundant recipient_name parameter (the true workflow derives the email as {customer}@example.com), omits the new-tab and tab-switching steps, and leaves the "not supported" case and the {version} extraction vague, so an automation built from it could mistakenly send the email.
